createdBy: cpm-6c (peer worker session field report, verified in code by codex-claude-bridge-dc)
impact:
There is no `tier` parameter on any MCP tool — `grep -rn "tier" src/tools/` returns nothing. The tier selector is a VALUE of the `model` parameter (`model: "max"`), but TIER_HELP, which is embedded in the `model` field's own description, reads: 'Or pick a tier instead of a model id: "max" ... "balanced" ... "fast"'. A caller who reads that text and passes `tier: "max"` has done the natural thing and is wrong; `registerTool`'s inputSchema is a plain Zod shape, so the unknown key is stripped by default rather than rejected, with no error and no warning. The call proceeds with no model selector at all, `requested` is `null`, and Gemini's unpinned default (`fast` tier, Flash (Medium) — ISS-052) serves the review.

Field evidence from cpm-6c (CPM worker session, 2026-09-18): `tier: "max"` was passed on every call in the session including all six that landed on Flash; it never influenced routing and `requested` stayed `null` throughout. Adding `model: "max"` on a later call — same session, same cwd, same `tier` argument still present — flipped to Gemini 3.1 Pro (High) immediately. The two arguments were the only difference. Consequence: a plan review went revise/revise on Pro and then approve/approve on Flash after the silent downgrade — the weaker model overturning the stronger one, with nothing in the response saying so except a model label the caller had to think to check. They did not bank the approves only because they were inspecting `models[].observed` every round.

From the caller's side, a dropped selector is indistinguishable from a bridge that has no stronger model available, which is precisely the wrong conclusion to lead someone to.

REPORTER'S PREFERRED FIX (cpm-c6, after confirming the root cause): reject unknown top-level arguments with an error that NAMES the accepted ones, on the grounds that a silently-dropped selector is the exact shape that produced a false gate here. Design consideration before adopting: strict rejection changes behavior for any caller currently passing extra keys, so weigh a hard error against a warning-plus-echo, and check whether any MCP client injects fields of its own.

Other fixes to consider: accept `tier` as a real alias that feeds the same resolver `model` does; rename or reword TIER_HELP so the parameter name and the concept name match; make `requested: null` distinguishable from "something was asked for and discarded" by echoing the dropped argument. Related: ISS-052 (the default that fills the vacuum), ISS-053 (no floor once a tier IS expressed).
internal_precedent: The config layer already does the right thing one layer down: config/loader.ts warnUnknownConfigKeys() walks the parsed config at every level and warns on stderr for each key the schema strips ("ignoring unrecognized config field(s) in <loc> (<path>): <keys>"), explicitly so a stale field surfaces instead of being an invisible no-op. Tool arguments have no equivalent. Adopting the same posture at the tool boundary is therefore consistency with an existing in-repo convention, not a new policy — and the stderr-only constraint (stdout carries JSON-RPC) already has a worked solution there.
resolution: Fixed on branch fix/iss-054-tool-arguments (2026-09-18), unreleased. Root cause confirmed: tool inputSchemas were raw Zod shapes, so the SDK parse stripped unknown keys before the handler could see them, and TIER_HELP said "pick a tier" inside the `model` field. Fix, per the owner's rule "understand what we can, proceed and tell the caller what we ignored, refuse only when proceeding would be the wrong review": (1) new src/tools/tool-input.ts — tools parse z.looseObject and classify every unknown key exactly once: FOLD an alias/camelCase/near-miss (edit distance 1 for names <=4 chars, 2 otherwise, unique nearest, value must validate against the target) into the real parameter and report argument_corrections; ECHO anything else in ignored_arguments + accepted_arguments and proceed; REFUSE (INVALID_INPUT, pre-provider, with the fold hint) only when the value is a model selector — tier word, known model id, or "latest" — and neither model nor tier was given. review_status/review_history fold or echo only. (2) `tier` is a real parameter (ReviewTierSchema enum) on the three review tools and `--tier` on the CLI, folded into the single selector backends take; model + tier together is INVALID_INPUT; the resume guard covers the folded selector. (3) TIER_HELP reworded; MODEL_PARAM_HELP / TIER_PARAM_HELP name each other. (4) The three report fields are host metadata in HostReviewMetadataFields and omitted from every model-facing response schema (guarded by the RESPONSE_SCHEMAS required-coverage test). Non-breaking: a stray key keeps working and is echoed; only the selector-intent case is a new refusal, and it replaces a wrong review. Advertised JSON schema now carries tier as an enum. Tests: 20 unit (tool-input.test.ts) + tool-level regression per tool including the reported `tier: "max"` shape, refusal asserting no provider/preparation call, echo on empty-capture paths, CLI --tier parity; full suite 1352 green, tsc/eslint clean, tsup build ok. Not done here: version bump/release (1.9.0 is the right number — additive, non-breaking). Related still open: ISS-052 (default tier), ISS-053 (floor), ISS-055 (review_mode naming).
title: Unknown tool arguments are silently stripped, and TIER_HELP invites the exact mistake: `tier: "max"` is accepted, dropped, and never reaches the resolver
